title: Difficulty across a shared text
statement: Should questions that share one text sit at one difficulty level, or span easy to hard like a quiz?
detail: The evaluator first routed sets of questions on one shared text through its quiz rules, which need all three difficulty levels present and no level above 60%, and the generator specification still requires that spread. A later dedicated evaluator expects uniform difficulty and fails a set only for wildly inconsistent levels. Both positions coexist in this snapshot: the committed half of the classifier sends such sets to the dedicated evaluator, while its stashed half still routes them to the quiz rules.
against: The generator specification's pipeline still routes such sets through the quiz rules: "Classifier fast-path → ContentType.QUIZ" (`icloud-work/incept/inceptbench/docs/MCQ_SET_PASS_SPEC.md`, line 13).

evidence.quote: - All three difficulty levels present (Easy, Medium, Hard)
Unlike quizzes which require Easy/Medium/Hard distribution, MCQ sets are expected to have UNIFORM difficulty - all questions should be at the same appropriate difficulty level.
# MCQ set → dedicated evaluator (uniform difficulty expected, unlike quizzes)
# MCQ set → classified as quiz (decomposed into individual MCQs)
